shortDescription: An inheritable Storageborn xenotype with sleeping-spot-only sleep and assignment, visible bodies while sleeping, configurable body-selection modes, age-scaled carrying and armor, body-specific generated names, Show Me Your Hands compatibility, an optional Ideology warning letter, and a refuge quest.
body:
## Storageborn xenotype and assets
- Adds inheritable xenotype `omw_storageborn`, membership gene `OMW_Storageborn`, custom head gene `OMW_StorageHead`, fourteen active body genes, and five age-stage genes. Requires Biotech, Big and Small - Genes and More (`redmattis.bigsmall.core`), and Vanilla Expanded Framework; loads after Harmony, Alpha Genes, Big and Small, and Show Me Your Hands when present, and before 10x Carrying Capacity.
- Membership gene applies pawn setup, suppresses visible tattoos, and selects a subtype. The xenotype is non-combatant and inheritable, with Big-and-Small diet, unliving, reproductive, clothing/equipment, resilience, pain, sensory, temperature/toxic, sleep, armor, movement, and skill-affinity genes. Thought nullifiers remove inappropriate apparel, beauty, sleeping, food, social, title-room, and corpse penalties.
- Harmony prefixes on `RestUtility.CanUseBedEver` and `CompAssignableToPawn_Bed.CanAssignTo` allow Storageborn pawns to use and be assigned only to `SleepingSpot`, `DoubleSleepingSpot`, or, with Biotech, `BabySleepingSpot`. Other beds fail use checks and bed assignments return a localized rejection.
- Shared render patches set the bed render body's visibility flag and override `PawnRenderNodeWorker_Body.CanDrawNow` for sleeping Storageborn, bypassing the bed's `bed_showSleeperBody` gate while retaining vanilla NoBody flags, explicit duty overrides, and node debug visibility. Vanilla pose and orientation remain in use; no individual bed defs are patched.
- Optional Show Me Your Hands integration detects its `HandDrawer.PostDraw` type at runtime and prefixes it to skip all hand rendering for pawns with `OMW_Storageborn`; it adds no hard dependency and safely does nothing when that mod is absent.
- Custom head renders `Head/StoragebornHead` via `PawnRenderNode_AttachmentHead`, with bald/no-beard filters and Big-and-Small facial-disabling support. Big-and-Small `PawnExtension.bodyPaths` supplies directional bodies and disables facial animation. Textures include body forms, head/eye art, and xenotype icon. Audio assets are not used.

## Body forms, custom extensions, and settings
- Six extensible categories: Neolithic, Medieval, Industrial, Spacer, Ultra, and Archotech. Fourteen active subtypes: Luggage, Mimic, Cardboard, Maid, Cube, Treant, Golem, Suitcase, Wardrobe, Orb, MechLoader, Cube2, Robot, and Robot2. Categories and categorized genes are discovered from loaded defs for extension by compatible mods. Test body defs in `GenesBodyTest.xml` are commented out and are not active.
- `StoragebornBodyGenesExtension` optionally lists genes added as endogenes when a body gene is added. Created genes are tracked on that body-gene instance and removed on `PostRemove`; unresolved references are logged. `StoragebornBodyBackstoriesExtension` optionally chooses one valid childhood background on add, preserving the default when absent/empty.
- `StoragebornBodyNameRulesExtension` optionally references a `RulePackDef`; when the corresponding body gene's `PostAdd` runs, it generates a first and last name from that pack and retains the pawn's existing nickname. The Neolithic fantasy Treant uses a plant/tree name list; the Golem uses a stone/rock name list.
- Body icons in the settings tab have tooltips listing bundled genes, or a localized empty state. Settings Body tab has a dropdown with Per category (default), Per body, and Follow World Tech Level (only offered when World Tech Level is available). Switching into Per category or Follow World Tech Level clears individual body-weight overrides so all body controls return to weight 1. Per category displays category toggles and all body types, per body displays probability sliders grouped by category, and Follow World Tech Level displays bodies in categories at or below world tech level. Body subtype relative weights range 0–1; zero excludes, positive values are normalized for random selection. Settings include effective-status explanations and rerolling discovered Storageborn pawns across maps, caravans, and world pawns. Missing weights default to 1. Body-gene selection preserves an existing gene that remains eligible unless forced; any other body genes are removed as duplicates. Explicit rerolling forces a new selection. Storageborn pawns also receive a dev-mode-only gizmo to force-reroll their body type. No eligible subtype logs an error and falls back to Wardrobe, or leaves existing genes unchanged if the fallback def is absent.
- Five stage offsets/factors edit `CarryingCapacity` and optional `VEF_MassCarryCapacity`; settings persist through ModSettings/Scribe. Reset restores defaults and reapplies stage stats.
- When Ideology is active and the player's primary ideology has a preferred-apparel precept targeting the upper or full head, a localized negative event letter warns once on new-game start. Its shown flag is saved with the world, so reloading does not repeat the warning.

## Life stages and refuge quest
- Setup assigns `OMW_StoragebornChildhood` fallback, removes worn apparel from babies, and calculates stage and armor genes. It does not assign a Wanderer adulthood backstory. Harmony postfix on `Pawn_AgeTracker.BirthdayBiological` refreshes lifecycle stages: baby/under 8, child from 8, adult from 18, large from 30, and gigantism at 50/70. Stage genes adjust carrying capacity; stages 0/1 exclude Tiny and reduce market value. Armor stages use Big-and-Small tough-skin/natural-armor genes.
- Adds hidden auto-accepted wanderer-joins quest and `OMW_StoragebornWanderer` incident, targeting player-home maps. Its pawn generator sets the Storageborn xenotype and runs setup. Incident eligibility is controlled by the Refuge quest setting, enabled by default.
- Dev action `Pawns -> Spawn Storageborn Lifecycle` creates player-owned test pawns at ages 0, 8, 18, 30, 50, and 70. Ships localized settings/scenario strings and compatibility, known-issue, design, and AI disclosure documentation.
